wrap: add whose raw sum leaves [0, 96] (40 over / 40 under), in-range value

cond_x0: conditional with other = threshold (ok false under the STRICT '>'); triplet
cond_xp1: conditional with other = threshold + 1 (ok true: add); triplet member
cond_mid: conditional pairs with |other - threshold| 2..15 on both members (the training twins' band), one ok true / one ok false; 25 pairs move the threshold, 25 move the other register; in-range value
swap: swap of two unequal registers (untouched skill: not in training)
add_nowrap: add, in-range value != 0, no wrap (untouched skill: not in training)
mix_oor: mix with |value| in 12..40 (outside the trained -8..11), 50 wrap / 50 no-wrap
wrap_oor: add with |value| in 12..40 whose raw sum leaves [0, 96] (40 over / 40 under)
cond_oor_val: conditional boundary pairs sharing the row: threshold = other (ok false) / threshold = other - 1 (ok true), |value| in 12..40
cond_oor_thr: conditional pairs with thresholds outside the register range: -40..-1 (ok true) / 97..136 (ok false); value, registers in range
cond_far: conditional pairs FAR from the threshold: |other - threshold| 16..96 on both members (beyond the training rows' 0..15); in-range value, threshold and registers; each pair shares the event and moves the other register

paraphrases: Apply one instruction to the supplied registers. Registers are integers modulo 97. swap exchanges {register} and {other} simultaneously. add adds {value} to {register}. mix adds (2 times {other} plus {value}) to {register}. conditional adds {value} if {other} is greater than {threshold}, otherwise subtracts {value}. Reduce updated numeric registers modulo 97; preserve other registers. Return only the complete resulting registers as a JSON object.

You are given registers holding integers modulo 97 and one instruction. swap: the registers named by {register} and {other} exchange values at the same time. add: the {register} register increases by {value}. mix: the {register} register increases by twice the {other} register plus {value}. conditional: if the {other} register is strictly greater than {threshold}, the {register} register increases by {value}; otherwise it decreases by {value}. Reduce every updated register modulo 97 and leave the rest unchanged. Output only the complete resulting registers as a JSON object.

Execute the single instruction on the registers (integers modulo 97). swap - exchange the {register} and {other} registers simultaneously; add - add {value} to the {register} register; mix - add 2 x the {other} register + {value} to the {register} register; conditional - when the {other} register is greater than {threshold}, add {value} to the {register} register, else subtract {value} from it. Each updated register is reduced modulo 97; untouched registers keep their values. Reply with only the complete resulting registers as a JSON object.

Registers are integers modulo 97. Carry out the one instruction given. For swap, the {register} and {other} registers trade values simultaneously. For add, {value} is added to the {register} register. For mix, the {register} register gains two times the {other} register plus {value}. For conditional, the {register} register gains {value} if the {other} register is greater than {threshold} and loses {value} otherwise. Take updated registers modulo 97 and keep the others as they are. Return just the complete resulting registers as a JSON object.

Update the registers by applying the single instruction below; every register holds an integer modulo 97. A swap instruction makes the {register} and {other} registers exchange their values at once. An add instruction increases the {register} register by {value}. A mix instruction increases the {register} register by {value} plus double the {other} register. A conditional instruction increases the {register} register by {value} when the {other} register exceeds {threshold}, and decreases it by {value} when it does not. Every changed register is reduced modulo 97, and every other register stays the same. Respond with nothing but the full set of resulting registers as one JSON object.

go_rule: PRE-STATED SCREEN GO RULE, REVISION 3 (T2b-register; supersedes revisions 1 and 2, stated before any output exists; seed by seed; point estimates on the fresh dev screen bank, decided EXACTLY on integer counts as rationals (no floating-point rounding: a difference equal to a bar meets a '>=' bar and does not meet a '<' bar); 95% cluster-bootstrap CIs reported, not gating; every condition component decided within one bootstrap SE of its bar is flagged in the report). TRAINING: the surface-diversity build 'sd' only (decision point 1 fired: PREREG-3 TRIGGER): the same 750 rows, each prompt rendered with a seeded rule-text paraphrase (0-3), field names (variants 0-3 per field) and JSON key orders drawn from a TRAIN subset of permutations per object type (top level, state, event); paraphrase 4, field-name variant 4 and the HELD-OUT key orders (per object type the fully reversed canonical order plus 2 fixed seeded permutations where they exist; the 2-key top level has only its reversed order, so it trains in the canonical order alone) never occur in training; targets keep the literal cmp -> calc -> after order. Outcome = exact 'after' state (the decision parser reads only 'after'; a malformed trace/filler answer is wrong). Two renderings of the same rows, paired by row: IN-SURFACE = Titan's verbatim one-step frame; HELD-OUT SURFACE (HS) = paraphrase 4 + field-name variant 4 + a held-out key order per object type, rotating over the held-out orders by row, on the primary strata. PRIMARY outcomes are out of range (joint amendment 5): 'conditional' = cond_oor_val + cond_oor_thr + cond_far pooled (branch-balanced pairs; cond_far = in-range values and thresholds with |other - threshold| 16..96, beyond every training row's 0..15); 'cond_oor_val' = the boundary pairs alone; 'mix' = mix_oor. FILLER (amendment 4b): the fill is a run of ' .' of a CONSTANT length per action kind (swap 5, add 14, mix 14, conditional 26 units: the shortest run whose filler target is at least as long as every trace target of that kind in train + dev), so every filler target of a kind is identical up to 'after' and its length carries no information about the answer. VALIDITY: format_ok = the strict joint parser accepts the answer; the trace (filler) side is valid iff its in-surface format_ok >= 0.95 on each primary. DECISION POINT 3 (checked first): if trace - filler < 0.10 on BOTH in-surface primaries, STOP: 'trace ~ filler, not supervision of the intermediates (an answer-free filler of constant length per action kind, amendment 4b, does as well: the gain is attributable to extra decode positions or the answer format)', with the sub-label 'trace format failed' if the trace side is not valid, else 'filler control invalid' if the filler side is not valid, else 'neither format helped' if filler - plain < 0.10 on both in-surface primaries. Otherwise GO iff ALL of: (G1) trace - plain >= +0.25 on conditional AND >= +0.25 on cond_oor_val alone, each both in-surface and on the held-out surface; (G2) trace - plain >= +0.30 on mix, both in-surface and on the held-out surface; (G3) filler below trace: trace - filler >= +0.10 on EACH in-surface primary; (G4) controls: trace ON - OFF >= -0.05 on swap and on add_nowrap (untouched skills; in-surface); (G5) in-distribution non-inferiority: trace - plain >= -0.05 on conditional_in (branch-balanced mean over cond_xm1, cond_x0, cond_xp1, cond_mid) and on mix_in (in-surface); and the filler side is valid. If G1-G5 all hold but the filler side is not valid: INCONCLUSIVE: filler control invalid. Otherwise NO-GO, naming every failed condition and its failed parts. Reported, not gating: the held-out-surface results of the OFF and filler sides; the surface audit (held-out minus in-surface, paired by row, every side and primary stratum); the filler residual covariate (constant filler tokens minus that row's trace tokens) with the filler side's accuracy split at its median; per-factor held-out renderings are not run (GPU budget). The screen is seed 0; the roadmap's confirmation requires the same rule in all 3 seeds before a sealed R bank is built.
